title: Balanced lambda preserves the quotient augmentation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its valuation ring $A$. Let $g:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism. Use the completed coefficient ring sheaves $R_Z$, strict positive quotient functors $\mathrm{red}_{R,Z}$, module pullback $g_R^*$ and their specified quotient units $b_{Z,n}$ from [def-sfb-integral-pullback-strict-roos-data]. Let $a:(g_R^*)^{\mathrm{Tow}}\circ\mathrm{red}_{R,Y}\cong\mathrm{red}_{R,X}\circ g_R^*$ be an isomorphism of the actual module-valued strict tower functors satisfying the balanced-generator formula IsLambdaNormalized. For every $R_Y$-module $M$ and every index $n\in\mathbf N$ (quotient exponent $n+1$), $g_R^*(b_{Y,n,M});a_{M,n}=b_{X,n,g_R^*M}$. No flatness, boundedness, constructibility or completeness condition is imposed.

source.place: First paragraph and Comparison with the Stacks Project; Balanced lambda preserves the quotient augmentation

proof.text:
test the two module maps on scalar-extension generators. The quotient
augmentation sends h to h tensor 1. The normalization of lambda sends the inverse
image of this generator to the tensor of the inverse image of h with the transported
unit residue. The coefficient homomorphism preserves 1, so this is the augmentation
of the pulled module. The pullback adjunction and the sheafified tensor universal
property imply equality from these generator identities. This works for arbitrary
modules, including torsion modules; no flatness or completeness is used.

theorem integralLambdaQuotientAugmentation
    (a : T l E g ≅ U l E g) (ha : IsLambdaNormalized l E g a)
    (M : ModR l E Y) (n : ℕ) :
    (pullR l E g).map
        (((completedReductionModuleUnit (datum l E) Y).app M).app (op n)) ≫
        (a.hom.app M).app (op n) =
      ((completedReductionModuleUnit (datum l E) X).app ((pullR l E g).obj M)).app
        (op n)
